papers.title: Knsight: Self-Evolving Agentic System for Production Cloud Root Cause Analysis
papers.abstract: Cloud incident response increasingly relies on LLM agents that translate heterogeneous telemetry and natural-language alerts into operator-facing diagnoses. However, in production RCA workflows, LLM agents commonly serialize these structured signals into text, losing the temporal and topological structure that is critical for diagnosis. We present Knsight, an industry-deployed RCA agent that converts operational telemetry into chart-image canvases and uses a frozen multimodal LLM to reason directly over visual evidence. Knsight introduces Vision Recursive-of-Thought (V-RoT), an iterative diagnose-review-refine loop in which a Reviewer module inspects each canvas and decides whether to refine, zoom in, or stop. To adapt across recurring production failures, Knsight further converts Reviewer feedback into a shared, alias-substituted skill library used at inference time. Offline, on the OpenRCA benchmark, Knsight improves aggregate Correct by 7.0 points over the strongest text-only baseline and reduces timeouts from 117 to 11. Online, in a 90-day deployment across 1,284 production incidents, Knsight increases top-1 acceptance from 38.9% to 71.4% and reduces time-to-acknowledge and time-to-resolve by 59% and 32%, respectively.
papers.reason: 图像画布是诊断智能体的核心交互界面：Reviewer 根据画布决定细化、放大或停止，并将反馈转化为推理时复用的技能。相比纯文本基线，端到端结果支持整体设计，但未单独验证视觉循环或技能库的贡献。
papers.evidence: Knsight introduces Vision Recursive-of-Thought (V-RoT), an iterative diagnose-review-refine loop in which a Reviewer module inspects each canvas and decides whether to refine, zoom in, or stop.
papers.result: Offline, on the OpenRCA benchmark, Knsight improves aggregate Correct by 7.0 points over the strongest text-only baseline and reduces timeouts from 117 to 11.

papers.title: Tool-Making and Self-Evolving LLM Agents in Low-Latency Systems
papers.abstract: Production LLM agents often waste latency and reliability by regenerating code for the same procedural steps on every request. We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment. The tool-maker grounds synthesis in the live environment as it collects execution traces, observes backend schemas and values, generates candidate tools, and repairs them against labeled cases. At runtime, the production agent calls these tools directly and falls back to code generation only when needed. We deploy the approach in a Fulfillment Center alarm-triage system, where an agent diagnoses alarms against a 44-node SOP over heterogeneous metric backends. In production, tool calls reduce p50 latency by 42%. On 1500 historical alarms, they reduce end-to-end error rate by up to 53% by suppressing run-to-run variance in repeated steps. Because tools return compact structured verdicts, they also enable a simpler direct-call architecture, reducing p50 latency by a further 62% in a controlled ablation. Versioned tools also improve auditability and expose specification gaps and upstream data drift. Our results show that agents that build and maintain their own tool libraries, a key element of self-evolving agents, can make industrial LLM systems faster, more reliable, and easier to operate.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是让软件代理利用真实执行轨迹和带标签的测试反馈，生成、修复并维护可复用的版本化工具，以替代逐请求写代码。跨模型组件消融、留出集测试和生产对照支持其效果；残余错误分析明确了规范质量的限制，但跨业务泛化尚未验证。另有基于筛选轨迹的辅助微调，并验证了无工具时的回退能力。工具上线仍需人工审核，未展示改进机制自身的演化。
papers.evidence: We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment.
papers.result: In production, tool calls reduce p50 latency by 42%.

papers.title: Learning What Not to Forget: Long-Horizon Agent Memory from a Few Kilobytes of Learning
papers.abstract: Long-running language-model systems accumulate interaction history that outgrows the context window, so they must continually evict. When an eviction policy drops a task-critical detail, for example an access token issued at login or a path the next call needs, the action fails. We present LRE (Learned Relevance Eviction), a kilobyte-scale, CPU-only, language-model-free scorer that learns which units of history are task-critical and keeps them by verbatim extraction. Under a matched-budget comparison, in our experiment, no baseline dominates LRE on the accuracy-cost plane. On agents, LRE recovers 93% of the aggregate accuracy of keeping the entire history (41.1 vs. 44.0) and exceeds it by 27% on the simplest tasks, while requiring zero compressor calls and cutting the worst-case peak prompt by 52%. A controlled study trace shows LRE completes tasks where the others loop, finishing one such task in 37% fewer calls than keeping everything and solving 14 tasks where no other run policy does. On conversational memory, LRE outranks dense and token-pruning encoders at zero neural cost while being 295–1569× smaller in size. In downstream evaluation, LRE gives the best budgeted answer quality on LoCoMo reading 68% fewer tokens. Its supervision can also be annotation-free: training only on the system’s own behavior recovers 95% of the supervised scorer’s effectiveness. We argue that, because memory eviction in LLM agents is a fidelity problem, it requires a deployable proactive policy where the future query is unavailable and exact state is decisive, and that cheap learned relevance can be sufficient.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是用轻量学习式评分器主动淘汰交互历史，逐字保留影响后续行动的关键信息。在未来查询未知的条件下，等预算对照量化了任务准确率与提示开销之间的取舍；摘要未给出足以复现评分器的细节。
papers.evidence: We present LRE (Learned Relevance Eviction), a kilobyte-scale, CPU-only, language-model-free scorer that learns which units of history are task-critical and keeps them by verbatim extraction.
papers.result: On agents, LRE recovers 93% of the aggregate accuracy of keeping the entire history (41.1 vs. 44.0) and exceeds it by 27% on the simplest tasks, while requiring zero compressor calls and cutting the worst-case peak prompt by 52%.

papers.title: CapMem: A Benchmark for Caption-Based Episodic Memory in Egocentric Video
papers.abstract: Wearable assistants require episodic memory over egocentric video, yet current vision-language models face bounded frame budgets, growing visual-token costs, and long-context retrieval failures. Under these practical constraints, we study whether textual captions can serve as reusable episodic memory. We define the Episodic Memory Video Caption QA task and introduce CapMem, a human-annotated benchmark with 75 videos totaling 33.7 hours, and 1,000 multiple-choice questions across 16 scenarios. On long videos (>20 min), full-coverage CaptionQA with 30s and 60s caption windows outperforms direct VideoQA for 10/12 and 8/12 models, respectively. On the same video subset, a matched-frame control across six Qwen models retains mean accuracy gains of 3.22 and 2.55 points, respectively. Our caption-guided retrieve-and-verify harness further improves accuracy by up to 5.3 points. These results support the effectiveness of caption memory for episodic reasoning over long egocentric video.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是评估可穿戴助手如何复用第一视角视频的情景记忆，而非设计摄像系统。方法将视频分段转为带时间戳的描述，并在检索后用稀疏帧核验。等帧对照显示，超过20分钟的视频中，30秒窗口平均提升3.22个百分点；短视频上直接视频问答通常更强，且受控结果限于Qwen模型。
papers.evidence: We define the Episodic Memory Video Caption QA task and introduce CapMem, a human-annotated benchmark
papers.result: On the same video subset, a matched-frame control across six Qwen models retains mean accuracy gains of 3.22 and 2.55 points, respectively.

papers.title: TSHMem: A Temporal-Semantic Hierarchical Memory Graph for Long-Term Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: Long-term conversational agents often face time-sensitive queries, requiring evidence that is both contextually relevant and valid for a specific time, event, or factual update. However, noisy temporal-entity cues, weak coupling between temporal anchors and retrieval paths, and sparse long-tail evidence often lead memory systems to retrieve semantically similar but temporally invalid or outdated evidence. We propose TSHMem, a Temporal-Semantic Hierarchical Memory Graph for long-term conversational agents. TSHMem addresses noisy conversational evidence by organizing dialogue turns, self-contained statements, hierarchical summaries, and entities into a heterogeneous memory graph. To connect temporal constraints with retrieval paths, it parses temporal intent, activates query-relevant entities, resolves event-referenced constraints, and injects temporal relevance into graph transition probabilities. It then combines time-aware structural propagation with semantic matching and hierarchical ranking to retrieve compact evidence that is temporally valid, contextually relevant, and robust to sparse long-tail memories. Experiments on LongMemEval S* and LoCoMo show that TSHMem consistently outperforms strong retrieval and memory-agent baselines, achieving 66.3% accuracy on LongMemEval S*, with an absolute gain of 18.6% over the strongest baseline while retrieving fewer evidence tokens.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是为长期对话代理构建外部记忆图，并将时间约束纳入图转移概率，以检索对当前查询仍然有效的历史证据。摘要报告了量化基线比较，但未提供消融、复现细节或适用边界。
papers.evidence: To connect temporal constraints with retrieval paths, it parses temporal intent, activates query-relevant entities, resolves event-referenced constraints, and injects temporal relevance into graph transition probabilities.
papers.result: achieving 66.3% accuracy on LongMemEval S*, with an absolute gain of 18.6% over the strongest baseline while retrieving fewer evidence tokens.

papers.title: MAViQ: Memory-Augmented Visual Querying for Multi-Turn MLLM Jailbreaks
papers.abstract: Jailbreaks against multimodal large language models (MLLMs) typically operate through image-text inputs. After each target response, the attacker must decide how the new feedback should shape the next image-text query: which clues should be stated in the text, which should appear as visual evidence, and how the text should refer to the image.Existing multimodal attacks typically rely on fixed image-text pairs or candidate search, limiting their ability to adapt across turns.Text-only multi-turn attacks can adapt to prior responses, but they do not decide how response-derived clues should be expressed across image and text.In this paper, we formulate this missing step as \textit{trace-to-query realization} and propose \underline{M}emory-\underline{A}ugmented \underline{Vi}sual \underline{Q}uerying (MAViQ), a black-box framework that converts response-derived clues into visual and textual constraints, refines the query after observing the generated image, and propagates feedback to subsequent turns.Extensive experiments on two benchmarks across six target MLLMs show that MAViQ achieves average attack success rates (ASRs) of 70.60% on MM-SafetyBench and 82.13% on JailbreakV-mini, outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.90% and 8.32%, respectively. Our code is available at  https://github.com/jixingtian/Maviq.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是利用跨轮反馈调整图文查询的交互框架，明确区别于固定图文对和仅文本的多轮方法。两个基准、六个目标模型的结果提供了量化基线比较，但摘要未报告消融，也未证明系统存储了图像记忆。
papers.evidence: we formulate this missing step as \textit{trace-to-query realization}
papers.result: outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.90% and 8.32%, respectively.

papers.title: COLLABMEM: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Collaborative Memory Operations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly rely on persistent memory to coordinate role-specialized work. Correctness requires more than recalling a fact: the fact must reach the right role, remain hidden from unauthorized roles, carry the right source, and update when a more authoritative value appears. We introduce COLLABMEM, a diagnostic benchmark for collaborative memory operations. Its matched memory-only harness fixes the trace, target role, answerer, judge, and gold event, localizing errors to sharing, access, routing, provenance, conflict resolution, or retention. COLLABMEM contains 58 hand-authored scenarios (1,118 core probes), a 174-scenario scaled split (3,359 probes), adversarial and compositional hard sets, and six transactive-memory competencies. We also propose TMS-GRAPH++, a scope-aware graph memory framework with role-filtered views, writer/provenance structure, and temporal [CURRENT] marking. Across five evaluation splits, TMS-GRAPH++ achieves the highest non-Oracle average score (69.6%). Evaluations using the official SDKs of Mem0, Letta, and A-Mem show that shared archives help, but reliable collaborative memory still requires explicit visibility, provenance, authority, and retention policies. We will release the dataset, evaluation code, and reproduced outputs to support future work on multi-agent memory systems.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是面向多智能体持久记忆的诊断基准。评测固定交互轨迹、目标角色、答题者、裁判和金标准事件，以定位共享、访问、路由、溯源、冲突消解和保留问题。所提图记忆在五个划分上的非 Oracle 平均分最高（69.6%），为显式设置可见性、来源、权威性和保留规则提供了设计依据；摘要未报告各机制的独立效果。
papers.evidence: We introduce COLLABMEM, a diagnostic benchmark for collaborative memory operations.
papers.result: Across five evaluation splits, TMS-GRAPH++ achieves the highest non-Oracle average score (69.6%).

papers.title: SWE-MEM: Learning Adaptive Memory Management for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon software engineering agents often need to manage lengthy and noisy interaction histories under limited context budgets. Existing memory management methods rely on static compression workflows or rigid compression schedules, and often decouple memory decisions from task-solving performance. We present SWE-MeM, a training framework for proactive and on-demand memory management in software engineering agents. SWE-MeM provides a flexible memory tool that lets agents decide when, what, and how to compress based on trajectory state, task progress, and remaining context budget. We train agents with synthesized proactive memory-management trajectories and Memory-aware GRPO, which jointly optimizes memory management and issue resolution through memory-aware trajectory splitting and step-level credit assignment. On SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-MeM achieves 43.4% and 60.2% resolve rate with 4B and 30B models, respectively, outperforming existing memory management baselines in both performance and efficiency.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是让软件工程智能体根据任务进度和上下文预算，自主决定何时压缩交互历史、保留什么以及如何压缩，以支持后续行动。摘要报告了解决率及相对基线的优势，但未提供消融或量化效率权衡。
papers.evidence: SWE-MeM provides a flexible memory tool that lets agents decide when, what, and how to compress based on trajectory state, task progress, and remaining context budget.
papers.result: On SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-MeM achieves 43.4% and 60.2% resolve rate with 4B and 30B models, respectively, outperforming existing memory management baselines in both performance and efficiency.

papers.title: AtomMem: Learnable Dynamic Agentic Memory with Atomic Memory Operation
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents increasingly face tasks that require reasoning over extremely long range. A key bottleneck is memory design: most prior approaches treat memory as a static, human-designed component, limiting adaptability. Inspired by biological memory evolution, we propose AtomMem, a framework that exposes a set of atomic memory operations—including summarization and CRUD primitives—as tool-like actions. The agent learns a policy over these operations purely via reinforcement learning, using only the task reward. AtomMem allows the agent to dynamically interleave summarization and CRUD to retain important information while managing memory efficiently. We evaluate AtomMem on streaming long-context understanding and web-navigation benchmarks, demonstrating an average improvement of 8.5 points over static memory workflows and 2.1 points over the current learnable-memory baseline. Ablation studies show that both summarization and CRUD are essential to train agent memory. The project can be accessed at https://github.com/RUCBM/AtomMem.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是让智能体学习何时用摘要和 CRUD 操作保留或修订外部记忆。两类基准上报告了相对静态及可学习基线的平均增益；摘要未给出消融效应量或适用边界。
papers.evidence: we propose AtomMem, a framework that exposes a set of atomic memory operations—including summarization and CRUD primitives—as tool-like actions.
papers.result: demonstrating an average improvement of 8.5 points over static memory workflows and 2.1 points over the current learnable-memory baseline.

papers.title: LatticeMind: A Conflict-Aware Memory Primitive for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems often fail not for lack of candidate answers, but because they have no persistent mechanism for deciding which incompatible claim should currently be trusted. Majority vote, debate, and judge-based selection choose an output without recording which claim wins, which is contested, or why a later update supersedes it. We present LatticeMind, a conflict-aware structured memory that handles contradiction at write time. It maintains explicit item status, applies cheap symbolic conflict checks, and routes the flagged cases to an LLM reconciler. On a label-blind ConflictBank evaluation that removes source-name hints, over a uniform draw of 200 examples from the full benchmark pool, LatticeMind reaches 0.965 accuracy versus 0.525 for the strongest baseline, with every gap significant at p<10^{-24} by paired McNemar test. Ablations show that removing the checker or the reconciler costs 12 to 14 points. Our claims are scoped to credibility conflicts, where one claim should defeat another: the coordination branch of the design is a safety override that we do not validate empirically, and all prompt-based comparisons are conditioned on a single backbone. On three secondary planning benchmarks and one synthetic scheduling diagnostic the picture is mixed: LatticeMind beats naive merge on three of four, but does not replace deliberation methods on tasks rewarding iterative search.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是面向多智能体的持久化共享记忆：在写入时用符号检查和选择性 LLM 裁决处理冲突，记录条目状态与来源，供后续智能体读取。文中给出更新规则和伪代码；单骨干、去除来源标签提示的对照评测中，准确率为 0.965，对照组最高为 0.525。消融支持裁决器的作用，但检查器的差异未达常用显著性阈值（p=0.07）。等预算的软件状态跟踪和混合的规划结果界定了适用范围；协调分支未获验证。
papers.evidence: We present LatticeMind, a conflict-aware structured memory that handles contradiction at write time.
papers.result: LatticeMind reaches 0.965 accuracy versus 0.525 for the strongest baseline

papers.title: To Answer or to Abstain: Mitigating Search-Agent Hallucinations via Abstention-Aware Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in equipping Large Language Models (LLMs) with search tools and outcome-reward reinforcement learning (RL) have achieved new state-of-the-art results on open-domain QA tasks. However, we argue that current training paradigms harbor a critical vulnerability: they predominantly reward correct answers but fail to penalize fabricated ones when retrieval fails, thereby implicitly exacerbating hallucinations. To address this, we propose Abstention-Aware Reinforcement Learning (AWA-RL), which dynamically shapes the abstention reward utilizing the model’s query-specific prior capabilities and continuous on-policy training observations. We also introduce a novel metric, RA-F1, to measure the capability-reliability trade-off. Compared to non-abstaining baselines, AWA-RL boosts absolute precision by up to 10.3% and overall RA-F1 by 2.9%, with only marginal sacrifice in raw accuracy. These results confirm that AWA-RL successfully yields highly capable and reliable search agents.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是根据查询级先验能力和在线策略训练观测动态调整弃答奖励，从而更新文本搜索代理的应答策略。相对不弃答基线，精确率和 RA-F1 均有量化提升，但摘要未给出原始准确率降幅或适用边界。
papers.evidence: dynamically shapes the abstention reward utilizing the model’s query-specific prior capabilities and continuous on-policy training observations
papers.result: Compared to non-abstaining baselines, AWA-RL boosts absolute precision by up to 10.3% and overall RA-F1 by 2.9%, with only marginal sacrifice in raw accuracy.

papers.title: TRACE: A Unified Rollout Budget Allocation Framework for Efficient Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is a promising approach for enhancing reasoning and agentic behavior in large language models. However, rollout-intensive policy optimization is often limited by insufficient reward contrast, arising when overly simple or complex prompts generate low-variance feedback and when outcome-only rewards assign the same terminal assessment to every decision in a multi-turn rollout. Past efforts have focused on allocating available rollout resources to promising prompts, yet they only leverage sample informativeness at the prompt level and neglect variation in prefix-level informativeness across turns within the same rollout. This work targets multi-turn agentic RL by modeling each ReAct-style thought-action-observation turn as a semantically distinct node, allowing budget allocation to extend from prompt roots to turn-level prefixes with further continuations, which naturally forms tree-structured rollouts. We introduce Tree Rollout Allocation for Contrastive Exploration (TRACE), a unified rollout allocation framework that enhances reward contrast within a fixed sampling budget. Technically, TRACE allocates rollout budget to both prompt roots and intermediate prefixes that are most likely to yield mixed terminal rewards. A shared generalizable predictor estimates conditional success probability at these anchors from prefix histories to guide this allocation. The resulting adaptive tree structure enriches outcome-only feedback and amplifies the policy-update signal. Empirically, TRACE achieves competitive performance and efficiency gains on typical agentic benchmarks, e.g., improving Qwen3-14B Multi-Hop QA average accuracy by 2.8 points over competitive baselines at equal sampling cost. Code is available at https://github.com/gfyddha/TRACE.
papers.reason: TRACE 将多轮 ReAct 强化学习的采样预算从提示根节点扩展到中间轮次前缀，用预测的成功概率挑选更可能产生不同终局奖励的分支，以增强策略更新信号。在相同采样成本下，多跳问答平均准确率提高 2.8 个百分点；摘要未报告消融或适用边界。
papers.evidence: TRACE allocates rollout budget to both prompt roots and intermediate prefixes that are most likely to yield mixed terminal rewards.
papers.result: improving Qwen3-14B Multi-Hop QA average accuracy by 2.8 points over competitive baselines at equal sampling cost.

papers.title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
papers.abstract: Online web agents often augment a base actor with memory, workflow, or skill modules. These modules can improve performance, but they also consume test-time tokens, a cost rarely reported alongside the actor’s inference cost. We study online augmentation, where this overhead is paid on every task, and re-evaluate its benefits under a fixed total inference budget. We compare AWM, ASI, and ReasoningBank with a token-matched vanilla baseline that uses the same budget for additional actor steps. Across four WebArena domains and three models, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.4-mini, and Qwen 3.6-27B, the vanilla baseline matches or surpasses all three augmentation methods in aggregate success rate while often using fewer total tokens. We observe a similar trend on WorkArena-L1 with Qwen 3.6-27B, indicating that the effect extends to enterprise knowledge-work tasks. Our results suggest that skills and workflow memory can be useful in specific domains, but their apparent gains often vanish against a budget-matched actor. We further show that run-to-run variance materially affects outcomes and should be reported as a core evaluation criterion for online web agents.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是评估在线记忆与技能模块在固定推理预算下的价值，而非提出新记忆机制。等预算对照将模块开销转用于额外执行步骤；跨模型和任务的总体结果表明，不使用模块的基线持平或更优。摘要未给出具体效应量或模块适用的边界条件。
papers.evidence: We compare AWM, ASI, and ReasoningBank with a token-matched vanilla baseline that uses the same budget for additional actor steps.
papers.result: the vanilla baseline matches or surpasses all three augmentation methods in aggregate success rate while often using fewer total tokens.

papers.title: Elastic Horizon: Discovering the Effective Interaction Frontier in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Scaling the interaction horizon—the maximum number of environment interactions per episode—improves LLM agents on long-horizon tasks, and curriculum-based methods that progressively expand the horizon outperform fixed-horizon alternatives. However, existing schedules are open-loop: they monotonically increase the horizon until a manually specified maximum, with no mechanism to detect when further expansion stops helping. We propose the effective interaction frontier hypothesis: a dynamic boundary beyond which additional interactions yield diminishing returns while cost grows linearly. We then introduce Elastic Horizon, a closed-loop controller that tracks this boundary via the 90th percentile of successful trajectory lengths. On AppWorld and BFCL, fixed-horizon sweeps reveal clear saturation plateaus; Elastic Horizon stabilizes the horizon inside the saturation band from both under- and over-capacity initializations, attains the best success rates across 7B and 14B backbones, and saves up to 25% of per-step trajectory tokens. Our work shifts the paradigm from how to scale interaction horizons to when to stop scaling.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是用成功轨迹长度的 P90、探索余量和指数滑动平均，闭环调整软件智能体强化学习中的交互步数上限，而非按训练步数单向扩张。固定上限扫描与高低初值测试支持其收敛到任务相关的饱和区间；两项基准、两种模型规模上的对照显示成功率更高，AppWorld 单步轨迹 token 最多节省 25%。控制规则本身未随经验改进，不构成 RSI。
papers.evidence: We then introduce Elastic Horizon, a closed-loop controller that tracks this boundary via the 90th percentile of successful trajectory lengths.
papers.result: Elastic Horizon stabilizes the horizon inside the saturation band from both under- and over-capacity initializations, attains the best success rates across 7B and 14B backbones, and saves up to 25% of per-step trajectory tokens.

papers.title: Beyond Fresh Starts: Stateful Inference for Streaming ASR in Conversational Voice Agents
papers.abstract: Modern voice-agent systems rely on streaming speech recognition models that operate under stringent latency constraints. This study shows that, due to the limited memory constraints of real-time processing, these systems are adversely impacted by conversational phenomena such as long silences and backchannels. While many agentic pipelines mitigate this by resetting state at each turn, this approach discards vital context and impairs performance at turn onsets. We propose two state-management strategies that preserve cross-utterance context to reduce onset errors. In experiments with two state-of-the-art streaming models on two spoken dialogue benchmarks, our best method yields an average of 15-21% relative WER reduction at utterance onsets.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是将语音代理逐轮重置的识别状态改为跨话语保留，而非单纯优化识别延迟。两种流式模型在两个口语对话基准上的实验报告了话语起始处的词错误率下降，但摘要未给出两种策略的实现细节或适用边界。
papers.evidence: We propose two state-management strategies that preserve cross-utterance context to reduce onset errors.
papers.result: our best method yields an average of 15-21% relative WER reduction at utterance onsets.

papers.title: When Denser Credit Is Not Enough: Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Training
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents require reinforcement learning methods that can assign credit to intermediate decisions under sparse and delayed rewards. Recent group-based methods such as GiGPO improve over trajectory-level GRPO by constructing step-level advantages at repeated anchor states. However, we show that such dense credit can be statistically unreliable: under limited rollouts, rare but lucky actions may receive overly large advantages, producing divergent anchor bias and late-stage training oscillation. We propose Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization (ECPO), a critic-free policy optimization algorithm that calibrates step-level credit before policy updates. ECPO combines Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage, which groups rollouts by canonical actions and shrinks low-count estimates, with Variance-Gated Credit Weighting, which suppresses anchor states dominated by within-action noise. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B show that ECPO consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving GiGPO by +5.2/+7.3 success points on ALFWorld/WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B while adding only 0.1% additional advantage-computation overhead.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是用轨迹反馈改进长程文本智能体的策略更新。相较于 GiGPO，ECPO 按动作聚合轨迹、收缩低样本优势估计，并降低高噪声锚点的权重。摘要报告了两个环境中的量化基线对比，但未提供消融来分离两个机制的效果。
papers.evidence: ECPO combines Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage, which groups rollouts by canonical actions and shrinks low-count estimates, with Variance-Gated Credit Weighting, which suppresses anchor states dominated by within-action noise.
papers.result: improving GiGPO by +5.2/+7.3 success points on ALFWorld/WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B while adding only 0.1% additional advantage-computation overhead.

papers.title: Learning What to Retain: Gated-Memory Routing for Efficient Collaboration in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)–based multi-agent systems tackle complex reasoning by orchestrating how multiple agents are configured and how they collaborate. A central challenge is to adapt orchestration to the evolving collaboration state. Routing from the query alone cannot adapt to intermediate progress or errors, which hurts accuracy. Routing from the complete execution history supplies this missing context, but forces later decisions to process every prior step, including redundant or low-utility ones. This creates an execution-history overload that inflates cost. Effective orchestration instead requires a compact state that captures useful progress without accumulating redundant context. We propose Gated-Memory Routing, which conditions each decision on the query and a learned execution memory. A learned Memory Write Gate commits only non-redundant reasoning steps, and a learned Retrieval Gate supplies each agent a compact, relevant subset, so every decision conditions on a clean, informative state. At each step, the system selects the next role and backbone from this memory, while an Adaptive Halting Controller stops execution once the memory contains sufficient evidence for answering. Across five reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, our framework is both effective and efficient: it attains the best average accuracy, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.44 points, while reducing HumanEval inference cost by 31.9% relative to that baseline. Code is available at https://github.com/rajibrhasan/gated-memory-routing.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是用学习式写入门和检索门保存、筛选协作中的推理步骤，以指导后续路由与停止决策，而非直接使用完整历史。五项基准提供了相对最强基线的量化比较，但摘要未给出门控消融或适用边界。
papers.evidence: A learned Memory Write Gate commits only non-redundant reasoning steps, and a learned Retrieval Gate supplies each agent a compact, relevant subset
papers.result: it attains the best average accuracy, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.44 points, while reducing HumanEval inference cost by 31.9% relative to that baseline.

papers.title: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly expected to operate across heterogeneous task regimes that require distinct execution paradigms. This challenges fixed agent systems and motivates system-level meta-adaptation beyond isolated component updates. While existing works have adapted external harness or trained underlying reasoning policies, full-system adaptation remains insufficiently characterized. The adaptation space between structure and execution is rarely made explicit, and the compatibility between the external harness and the internal reasoner is not optimized jointly. We propose HarnessForge, a meta-adaptive framework for evolving LLM agent systems. HarnessForge formulates an agent system as a harness–policy pair, defining a stable adaptation space that separates harness-level execution structure from policy-level reasoning behavior. It then performs harness–policy co-evolution through fault-guided harness tailoring and harness-conditioned policy alignment. Experiments across five benchmarks from diverse domains show that HarnessForge consistently improves both Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B backbones, outperforming harness-only and policy-only baselines with gains of up to 12.0% over the strongest baseline and achieving favorable rollout-efficiency tradeoffs, demonstrating that harness–policy co-evolution is effective, and that executable compatibility between the harness and reasoning policy is essential for agent-system adaptation.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是利用故障反馈调整执行框架，并在更新后的框架下对齐推理策略。五个基准、两种模型规模上的实验报告称，联合演化优于仅调整框架或仅更新策略的基线，支持联合适配这一设计选择。摘要未给出可复现细节，也未表明改进机制本身得到改进。
papers.evidence: It then performs harness–policy co-evolution through fault-guided harness tailoring and harness-conditioned policy alignment.

papers.title: SIRI: Self-Internalizing Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Skills for LLM Agent Training
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can benefit from reusable skills, yet existing skill-based methods often rely on external skill generators during training or persistent skill retrieval at inference, increasing engineering complexity, context length, and deployment latency. We propose Self-Internalizing Reinforcement learning with Intrinsic skills (SIRI), a three-phase framework that enables agents to discover, validate, and internalize skills without external skill generators or inference-time skill banks. SIRI first warms up the policy with GiGPO to acquire basic interaction ability and collect successful skill-free trajectories. It then performs self-skill mining, where the current policy summarizes compact skills from its own successful plain rollouts and validates them through paired skill-augmented and skill-free rollouts. Finally, SIRI distills only beneficial skill-guided action tokens into the plain policy using trajectory-level utility and action-level advantage. At inference, the agent runs with the original prompt only. On ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, SIRI improves GiGPO from 0.908 to 0.930 on ALFWorld and from 0.728 to 0.813 on WebShop, outperforming prompt-based, RL-based, and memory-augmented baselines. Further analysis shows that our self-mining strategy can achieve performance comparable to distillation with closed-source large model.
papers.reason: 策略从自身成功轨迹提炼可复用技能，通过有无技能的配对试验筛选，再将有益动作蒸馏回策略。WebShop 的量化对照支持文本代理的策略改进；不计入 ALFWorld，也未证明改进机制本身得到提升。
papers.evidence: SIRI distills only beneficial skill-guided action tokens into the plain policy using trajectory-level utility and action-level advantage.
papers.result: from 0.728 to 0.813 on WebShop

papers.title: No Training, No Architecture Change: Per-Cell Warm-Up Calibration for LLM Agent Memory
papers.abstract: LLM agent memory modules universally adopt a single global retrieval depth k across all deployment scenarios; this global constraint produces an irreducible Oracle performance gap. We carry out a systematic evaluation on 19 heterogeneous deployment cells covering three LLM backbones, three multi-agent coordinators, three tasks, and two representative memory architectures (A-Mem and G-Memory). We confirm that the per-cell optimal k varies dramatically across cells, that low-capacity LLMs exhibit catastrophic accuracy collapse at larger k , and that no cross-cell feature or lookup-table shortcut reliably predicts the per-cell optimum. A theoretical analysis further shows that in the small-budget paired-binary-reward regime, every training-free bandit method we evaluate reduces to uniform-mean argmax. Motivated by this collapse, we propose per-cell warmup calibration: paired probe queries iteratively estimate the mean reward of each candidate k, the procedure commits to the empirical argmax, and a closed-form (2 σ) criterion provides earlystop. The recipe is training-free, requires no architectural modification, and introduces no hyperparameter beyond the probe budget. On all 19 deployment cells it attains 100% of the per-cell Oracle, with an average absolute improvement of +3.33 percentage points and a peak gain of +12.00 percentage points.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是将文本 LLM 智能体外部记忆的固定全局检索深度改为逐部署单元校准：用配对探测估计候选深度的平均奖励，并选择经验最优值。19 个部署单元的量化结果支持这一设计选择，但摘要未给出探测成本与收益的权衡。
papers.evidence: we propose per-cell warmup calibration: paired probe queries iteratively estimate the mean reward of each candidate k, the procedure commits to the empirical argmax, and a closed-form (2 σ) criterion provides earlystop.

papers.title: OrchDebate: Adaptive Orchestration for Multi-Agent Debate via Self-Evolving Skills
papers.abstract: Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) has emerged as a promising paradigm for eliciting stronger inference-time reasoning, yet most existing systems still use fixed interaction protocols across instances. Such static designs can suffer from anchoring bias, overthinking on easy problems, and rigid coordination across tasks of varying difficulty. We present OrchDebate, a framework that recasts multi-agent debate as structured-state orchestration over reusable debate-control skills. Instead of following a pre-defined template, OrchDebate uses an orchestrator to examine the current debate state and select the next coordination action, such as introducing agents under different visibility settings or terminating deliberation with an adaptive readout rule. This skill-based view makes debate control modular and state-dependent. The orchestrator operates through a structured control interface rather than directly generating reasoning content, helping reduce reliance on early answers. OrchDebate further maintains a self-evolving skill bank whose reusable realizations are refined through outcome-guided updates on an evolution stream, without additional external training data. Across diverse benchmarks, OrchDebate delivers a better accuracy-cost trade-off than representative fixed and adaptive debate methods by allocating debate compute more selectively.
papers.reason: 核心贡献之一是利用跨回合结果与状态诊断改写可复用的辩论控制技能，而非仅在单回合内动态编排。候选仅在后续回合试用，达到证据量、收益和退化率门槛后才替换原版本。GPQA 消融显示，关闭演化后三种模型的准确率均下降、词元开销均上升；固定技能库对照和信用权重敏感性测试进一步支持该结论。未显示生成或筛选改进的机制本身也在演化，因此不标 RSI。
papers.evidence: OrchDebate further maintains a self-evolving skill bank whose reusable realizations are refined through outcome-guided updates on an evolution stream, without additional external training data.

papers.title: Harnessing LLM Agents with Skill Programs
papers.abstract: Equipping LLM agents with reusable skills derived from past experience has become a popular and successful approach for tackling complex and long-horizon tasks. However, such lessons are often encoded as textual guidance that remains largely advisory, lacking explicit mechanisms for when and how to intervene in the agent loop. To bridge the gap, we introduce HASP (Harnessing LLM Agents with Skill Programs), a new framework that upgrades skills into executable Program Functions (PFs). Rather than offering passive advice, PFs act as executable guardrails that activate on failure-prone states and modify the next action or inject corrective context. HASP is highly modular: it can be applied at inference time for direct agent-loop intervention, during post-training to provide structured supervision, or for self-improvement by evolving validated, teacher-reviewed PFs. Empirically, HASP drives substantial gains compared to both training-free and training-based methods on web-search, math reasoning, and coding tasks. For example, on web-search reasoning, inference-time PFs alone improve the average performance by 25% compared to (multi-loop) ReAct Agent, while post-training and controlled evolution achieve a 30.4% gain over Search-R1. To provide deeper insights into HASP, our mechanism analysis reveals how PFs trigger and intervene, how skills are internalized, and the requirement for stable skill library evolution.
papers.reason: HASP 将文本技能转化为可在易错状态触发、修改下一步动作或注入纠正上下文的程序函数，并通过教师复核与验证迭代技能库。摘要报告了量化基线对比，但未单独量化技能演化的收益，也未表明改进机制本身得到改进。
papers.evidence: for self-improvement by evolving validated, teacher-reviewed PFs.
papers.result: post-training and controlled evolution achieve a 30.4% gain over Search-R1.

papers.title: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) based GUI agents stand to benefit significantly from online reinforcement learning (RL). However, their training is bottlenecked by two fundamental issues: current data synthesis methods for GUI Agents rely on specific environments and struggle to generate diverse data, while existing evaluators either suffer from limited scalability or provide inaccurate and unreliable reward signals. To overcome these challenges, we introduce GSAR (Goal-State-Anchor Reward), a RL reward framework that supports scalable task generation and delivers reliable reward signals for stable and efficient policy optimization. Our approach features self-evolving data synthesis, which produces multiple environments through task execution and generates diverse tasks and goal states. Complementing this, a state-anchor mechanism automatically annotates task-relevant UI elements in successful goal states as reference anchors. During RL training, these reference anchors provide accurate, scalable reward signals that substantially enhance efficiency. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves over 90% accuracy on offline trajectory verification and performs closest to rule-based methods. Furthermore, agents trained using our reward framework exhibit strong performance on both AndroidWorld and our constructed benchmark, establishing a scalable approach for GUI agent training.
